newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday July 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday July 10.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* In an interview, prime minister Romano Prodi said that the current parliament's term would end when the process of institutional reform had been completed, adding that his government would step down once a new electoral law had been approved (Corriere della Sera, "Sette" magazine).

* A report by national statistics institute Istat showed Italian industrial orders rose 14.5 percent year-on-year in April while turnover rose 9.1 percent. Industry minister Pierluigi Bersani said industrial orders and turnover data were good, but the country still had its work cut out to reach the government's economic growth target for this year. Trade unions and employers' association said they were not so confident the economy would pick up (all).

* The European Commission approved plan by the Italian government to recapitalise troubled flag-carrier Alitalia. Plans include financing for 2.75 trillion lire in three tranches provided Alitalia cut 1,200 jobs and sold its 35 percent stake in Hungarian national airline Malev (all)
* Pietro Ciucci, director general of state holding company IRI, said the group would clear its debts by the end of the year thanks to its ongoing privatisation programme (all).

* Public works minister Paolo Costa said the privatisation programme of motorway manager Autostrade had to be examined by the Italian Treasury. The group is expected to be valued at between 4.3 and 4.6 trillion lire and a selection of a stable core of shareholders with a 25 to 30 percent stake should be made by the end of July (all).
* Industry minister Pierluigi Bersani said that talks were in progress on a joint-venture between state-owned engineering group Finmeccanica and Britain's General Electric Co Plc (Sole 24 Ore).

* Agri-chemical group Compart said it would complete the sale of its Calcestruzzi unit to Italcementi by the end of July. Compart Calcemento holding company will receive a "financial benefit" of nearly 500 billion lire (all).

* Transport Ministry figures showed Fiat Auto new car registrations in Italy in June totalled 102,100, up 65.8 percent from June 1996. Industrial sources close to the group said Fiat's European market share rose in June to 13 pecent from 11.2 percent in June 1996 and and 12.9 percent in May (Sole 24 Ore).

* Transport minister Claudio Burlando said Italian new car registrations soared 50.71 percent in June to 222,800 units. Burlando also said that a car incentives scheme which has lead to a sharp recovery in registrations over the past six months should not be terminated abruptly (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
